title: The Falcon
paragraphs: Detective adventures centered on Michael Waring, known as the Falcon, who investigates murders and other crimes in a long-running series that changed lead actors and formats over time.

Detective series centered on Michael Waring, the radio Falcon. The radio Waring lineage derives from Drexel Drake and should not be collapsed into the separate RKO film Falcon identity. Frozen GRH corpus has 88 dated broadcasts, four undated program recordings, and ten reference/biography audio tracks.

GRH documents the program through Blue Network / Berry Kroeger (April 10, 1943 to December 18, 1943) on [[org|org.acb290b0843b31ec|Blue Network]], Mutual / James Meighan (November 27, 1945 to July 3, 1947) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], Les Tremayne era (July 10, 1947 to May 7, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and NBC/Kraft / Les Damon (May 14, 1950 to July 5, 1953) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Les Damon (performer on 52 recordings), Drexel Drake (creator on 50 recordings), Ed Herlihy (announcer on 42 recordings), Bernard L. Schubert (producer on 38 recordings and transcriber on 2 recordings), Richard Lewis (director on 37 recordings), Arlo (music on 28 recordings), and Eugene Wang (writer on 22 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).
Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include private investigation, murder and homicide, fraud and deception, and robbery and theft.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Distinct Falcon source lineages, Postwar private-eye radio culture, and Kraft-sponsored NBC era.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (12 shared credited people), [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (10 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (8 shared credited people), [[show|gang-busters|Gang Busters]] (9 shared credited people), and [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] (10 shared credited people).
